title: Gearbox
prompt: A labelled bench teaching cutaway of the pages 40 and 41 manual gearbox uses a hand-driven input, constant-mesh input pair, layshaft, freely rotating upper gears, output shaft, selector rods and forks, sliding collars with dog teeth, and a reverse idler. Drive turns the input and shows the selected torque path. Shift first disengages or stops the hand input, releases the previous dog engagement through neutral, selects one forward ratio, then allows drive to resume. Include direct input-to-output top gear. Reverse is selectable only with the input stopped and inserts the idler to reverse output rotation. See-through follows the gear pairs and engaged dogs. Do not slide the permanently meshed forward gear pairs out of mesh or engage two gears at once. Full synchromesh internals belong to the separately sourced synchromesh lesson.
blurb: A hand-driven teaching adaptation of the book gearbox selects constant-mesh dog ratios, direct top gear and a stopped-input reverse idler.
truthNotes: Teaching adaptation, not an exact reconstruction or verified edition union.
1998 and 2016 printed pages 40 and 41 were read from saved primary OCR.
Hand input replaces the engine. No clutch internals or full synchromesh are represented.
Forward wheel centers stay fixed. One selector engagement is permitted at a time.
Tooth flanks, dog phasing and dimensions are schematic rather than engineering drawings.
telemetry: No production telemetry is installed. Local verification only.
